transcript.text: lg w/d keeps saying dE n wont start?? door is shut

On LG washers/washer-dryers, dE usually means the machine isn’t detecting the door as properly closed/locked — even if it looks shut.

Try this:

1. Turn it off and unplug it for 5–10 minutes.
2. Open the door and check for:
• Clothing caught in the door seal
• A sock/item blocking the latch area
• Detergent buildup or debris around the door catch
• A damaged, loose, or bent plastic/metal latch hook on the door
3. Close the door firmly until you hear/feel a click. Don’t slam it hard or force the handle.
4. Plug it back in and try a cycle again.

Also make sure the machine is not overloaded; a bulky load can push against the door and prevent the lock engaging. Try starting it empty as a test.

If dE appears immediately every time, especially after cleaning/reseating the door, the likely issue is the door-lock assembly, door latch, or its wiring and it will need repair/service. Avoid repeatedly forcing the door closed, as that can break the latch further.

If you share the exact LG model number and whether it’s a front-load washer, combo washer-dryer, or dryer, I can narrow down the specific checks.
its an lg washer dryer, model FWV796WTSE. only happens w my mums king size duvet in, normal washes are fine. tried unplugging it, still dE

Because it only happens with the king-size duvet, the washer itself/door lock is probably OK. The duvet is likely pressing against the door or getting caught in the seal/latch area, so the lock cannot engage and the machine shows dE.

Try:

• Take the duvet out and run/try to start a cycle empty — if it starts, that confirms it’s load-related.
• Check the duvet isn’t trapped anywhere around the rubber door seal, especially near the latch side.
• Put it back in loosely, not tightly folded or packed against the door. Leave enough space for the drum to turn.
• Don’t add other laundry, towels, or detergent pods sitting in the door area.

A king duvet can be too bulky for a domestic washer even if it technically fits dry; once wet it becomes much heavier and expands. It may be better to use a laundrette/commercial large-capacity machine, particularly if it’s feather/down or a thick synthetic duvet.

Also check the duvet care label: many king duvets specify a larger drum capacity than a standard washer-dryer. And don’t try to dry it in the LG if it is already very tightly packed—washer-dryers generally have a substantially smaller drying capacity than their wash capacity.

If the machine starts normally with no duvet or ordinary loads, there’s unlikely to be a fault requiring repair.

ok checked, duvet is bulging against the glass and a corner is squashed in the rubber seal. door closes but springs back a bit. with the duvet out it starts fine. so what do i do, i need it washed before visitors come

Don’t try to force it or hold the door shut — the duvet is too large for the drum/door clearance, and it could damage the door lock, seal, or machine.

Your practical options are:

1. Use a laundrette with a large-capacity machine
   This is the best/safest solution. Look for a large washer (usually 14–18 kg or larger) and check the duvet’s care label first. Take it there dry if possible.

2. If it is inside a duvet cover, remove the cover
   Wash the cover at home separately. The actual duvet still needs enough empty drum space to move freely, but this may clarify whether you were trying to wash both together.

3. Use a temporary bedding alternative for visitors
   Wash the duvet cover and use spare blankets/throws, another duvet, or borrow one while the king duvet goes to a laundrette or dry cleaner.

Avoid washing it in the bath unless the care label explicitly permits it and you have a realistic way to dry it thoroughly. A wet king duvet is extremely heavy, difficult to rinse, and can develop mildew if it stays damp inside—especially down/feather filling.

The fact the washer starts normally with the duvet removed confirms the `dE` isn’t a machine fault; it is correctly refusing to lock with the load trapped in the seal.
